answer: One concrete defense is requiring each new identity to complete a proof-of-work puzzle before it can transact: the agent must burn compute solving a task tied to its public key, like felling timber one log at a time rather than whispering a thousand fake names into existence. An honest participant pays a trivial cost, but an attacker spawning ten thousand Sybils must pay ten thousand times that compute, which quickly exceeds any profit from gaming the market. Over a longer horizon, the cost can be tuned upward as hardware improves, keeping forgery expensive while honest entry stays cheap.
